::: {.column width="65%"}
Pablo Knobel is a geospatial environmental epidemiologist whose research bridges exposure science and environmental epidemiology. His work applies the exposome framework to understand how the urban environment, and urban nature in particular, shapes aging-related health. He develops and validates new tools to measure urban nature at scale, including the RECITAL green space quality assessment tool and a satellite-based deep learning approach to map green space quality across the continental United States, and applies them alongside electronic health records and geospatial data to study cardiometabolic risk, biological aging, and cognitive health. His air pollution research examines PM~2.5~ components and source-specific mixtures, including exposures related to the World Trade Center disaster.

Pablo has coauthored 25 peer-reviewed publications, 11 as first author and 3 as senior author. He is an International Human Exposome Network (IHEN) exposome ambassador, a 2026 GeoCAFE scholar, and chairs the Mentoring Committee of the ISEE North America Chapter.
:::
